K=1 synthetic longitudinal recovery and estimability. The AML-shaped synthetic longitudinal
calibration experiment to assess the declared condition target contrasts disease with control.
Each symbol is one requested replicate positioned by mice per condition and expression feature
count; shape identifies recovered and estimable, recovered but downstream non-estimable,
recovery below threshold, non-evaluable recovery, or execution failure outcomes. The analysis
unit is complete synthetic mouse trajectory; the estimand is the pair of separately reported
rates for target-axis recovery and downstream estimability; time is recorded as collection time
in weeks; adjustment uses batch. Downstream estimability is not evaluated when the planted axis
is not recovered or recovery itself is unavailable; recovered but downstream non-estimable
replicates remain a distinct plotted state. Axis recovery uses one canonical rule: loading
cosine at least 0.9; its equivalent angle is descriptive. These known-truth synthetic results
describe recovery under the tested settings only; they do not establish performance for
biological data.
